priorities.summary: SSRF flaw in the open-source project-management tool Plane (before 1.4.0): the webhook delivery task follows redirects without validation, so a workspace user can point a webhook at an attacker URL that redirects to internal resources (including cloud metadata) and exfiltrate responses via webhook logs. Fixed in Plane 1.4.0.

Missing authorization flaw in UTMStack (before 11.2.16): the command WebSocket handler applies no role check or command allowlist, so any authenticated user — regardless of role — can push arbitrary OS commands over gRPC to connected monitoring agents, where agent processes commonly run as root/SYSTEM.

Path traversal flaw in Fortinet FortiMail (versions 7.2.x–8.0.1) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker write arbitrary files to the underlying system via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests, enabling code/command execution. Confirmed exploited in zero-day attacks; added to CISA's KEV catalog on Oct 1 with an Oct 4 federal remediation deadline.

model.name: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk")
model.summary: Mistral's largest and most capable model to date — a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal MoE (49B active parameters) trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Europe, targeting coding, agentic workflows, cybersecurity, finance and law. Available now as a public preview with open weights promised for end of October; Mistral claims it leads open-weight models built outside China.
